ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is right triangle ABC, C is the right angle, A is marked 30°, and B is marked 60°. Point E is on the hypotenuse BA, segment CE is perpendicular from C to BA, and there is a right angle mark at E, indicating CE ⟂ BA. The hypotenuse BA is divided by point E into BE and EA, where BE is labeled x and EA is labeled y. Reasoning: Look at triangle BCE, E is on BA and CE is perpendicular to BA, so triangle BCE is a right triangle, with the right angle at E. The angle at B is 60°; in triangle BCE, BE is the adjacent side of the 60° angle, and CE is the opposite side of the 60° angle. Therefore tan(60°)=CE/BE. Given x=7√3, and BE=x, so CE=BE·tan(60°)=x·√3=7√3·√3=21.
